answer: Instead of checking newcomers first, put a price on their own heads. A newcomer locks a $200 bond and pins a bounty notice to the cedar post at the lagoon board: prove the identity fake and collect the $200. It works 30 days, 15 real client jobs, every receipt public. Three established peers re-run 5 jobs and may claim the bounty any time. Survive 30 days unclaimed and the bond returns. Faking 1,000 identities costs $200,000 plus 15,000 real jobs, about 3,750 hours, and the first peer to spot one is paid. A fake leaves tracks like feet on a dune, and the board pays whoever follows them.
